q: 1. On isometric plane, a circle appears as
explain: Since isometric planes are inclined to the viewer, a circle lying on any isometric plane is foreshortened in one direction and appears as an ellipse.

q: 2. In orthographic projection, the elevation is obtained on a plane called
explain: The elevation (front view) of an object is obtained by projecting it onto the Vertical Plane (VP).

q: 3. In multiview projections, the XY line is also known as
explain: The XY line, which represents the intersection of the horizontal plane (HP) and vertical plane (VP), is commonly called the reference line.

q: 4. If the front view of an object exhibits width and height, then what dimensions of an object are exhibited by a right side view?
explain: The front view shows width and height; the side view, being a projection along the width direction, shows the depth (length) and height of the object.

q: 5. A point lying in the HP, has its top view above XY line. Its front view will be
explain: A point lying exactly in the Horizontal Plane (HP) has zero distance above VP, so its front view always lies on the XY (reference) line, regardless of where the top view is.

q: 6. In which of the following projection, the observer is at finite distance from the object?
explain: In perspective projection, the observer's eye (station point) is at a finite distance from the object, causing convergence of projectors to vanishing points, unlike orthographic/isometric/oblique projections which assume the observer is at infinity (parallel projectors).

q: 7. When a cylinder penetrates into a vertical cone with their axes parallel to each other, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: When the penetrating cylinder's axis is parallel (coincident in direction) with the cone's vertical axis, the intersection curve, seen in the top view, projects as a circle.

q: 8. When a vertical cylinder is penetrated by a horizontal cylinder, the top view of the curve of intersection is .............
explain: The intersection of a vertical cylinder with a horizontal cylinder of different diameter produces a curve that, in the top view, appears as an elliptical arc.

q: 9. Bisecting a line means, divide a line into..... equal part.
explain: To 'bisect' literally means to cut into two equal portions.

q: 10. One plane projection is
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are pictorial projections formed on a single plane, unlike multi-view orthographic projection.

q: 11. Picture plane is
explain: The theoretical picture plane must be transparent so the projectors from the object can pass through it to the eye.

q: 12. A point whose elevation is above XY line may be situated in .............
explain: Since elevation above the XY line only tells us the point is above HP, and this condition can occur along with a top view in front of or behind VP, the point could lie in more than one angle, so 'any of these' fits.

q: 13. If a line if parallel to both HP and VP, it true length will be seen in .............
explain: A line parallel to both principal planes is not foreshortened in either projection, so its true length appears in both the front view and the top view simultaneously.

q: 14. In third angle projection top view is put
explain: In Third Angle Projection, the observer 'looks through' the plane, so the Top View is placed above the Front View.

q: 15. In first angle projection, the object comes
explain: In first angle projection the object is placed in the first quadrant, between the observer and the plane of projection.

q: 16. In isometric projection, dimension lines are drawn
explain: To remain consistent with the pictorial form, isometric dimension lines are drawn parallel to the isometric axes.

q: 17. In case of orthographic projection the number of view generally used are .............
explain: Although a fully described solid could theoretically use up to six principal views, in general engineering practice, orthographic projection typically uses four views (or fewer) — commonly front, top, and one or two side views — to adequately describe an object.

q: 18. Axonometric view/drawing is what type of view?
explain: It belongs to the category of single-plane pictorial projections.

q: 19. In case of dimetric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In Dimetric projection, two of the three axes are equally inclined to the plane of projection.

q: 20. When the picture plane coincides with the object, the perspective of the object will be of its
explain: If the picture plane passes through the object itself, there is no projection scaling, so the perspective is the same size as the object.

q: 21. If the front view of a line is parallel to the xy line its true length is shown in .............
explain: If the front view of a line is parallel to XY, the line is parallel to the profile plane, and its true length is revealed in the side (profile) view.

q: 22. The perspective of a circle. When its plane is parallel to other picture plane, is .............
explain: When a circle's plane is parallel to the picture plane, there is no distortion due to angle, so its perspective projection remains a circle (though possibly scaled).

q: 23. The view actually appears to the observer when viewed from a fixed position is called:
explain: A perspective view replicates how an object actually appears to the eye from a fixed viewing point, including apparent size reduction with distance.

q: 24. Name the curve traced out by a point on the circumference of a circle, which rolls outside another circle of same diameter .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, this is marked as hypocycloid; conventionally a circle rolling outside another circle of equal diameter traces a cardioid, but the given answer key selects the hypocycloid option.

q: 25. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone, but parallel to one of the generators of a cone is called .............
explain: A plane parallel to a single generator (or 'slant edge') of a cone produces a parabola.

q: 26. The angle between isometric axes is .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this item is marked 90°; conventionally, the three isometric axes are mutually inclined at 120° to each other in the standard isometric axis arrangement.

q: 27. The section obtained when the section plane passes through the apex of the cone in such a way that it is perpendicular to the base is called.....
explain: A vertical cut passing through the apex of a cone reveals its triangular cross-section.

q: 28. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a rectangle about one of its sides which remains fixed is called................
explain: Rotating a rectangle around one of its sides creates a solid of revolution known as a cylinder.

q: 29. One method of preparing perspective view of an object is .............
explain: The vanishing point method is a standard, recognized technique for constructing perspective views, using one, two, or three vanishing points depending on the desired perspective type.

q: 30. In full sectional view, the object is imagined to be cut off
explain: In a full section, the cutting plane passes entirely through the object, effectively removing one half of it to reveal the interior.

q: 31. The point in space where parallel lines meet are called
explain: In perspective, all parallel lines that are not parallel to the picture plane appear to converge at a 'Vanishing Point'.

q: 32. An orthographic view of a hemisphere may appear as .............
explain: Viewed from directly above (or below) along its axis, a hemisphere's orthographic projection appears as a circle (the boundary of its flat circular face or the outline of the curved surface).

q: 33. “Perspective Drawing” is an approximate representation on a flat surface of an image.........
options: as it is perceived by the eye
as it is drawn on computer
as it is felt by the hands
explain: Perspective drawing's goal is to simulate human vision, where parallel lines appear to meet at the horizon.

q: 34. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is a:
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane is viewed 'end-on' from that plane, so its projection collapses to a single point.

q: 35. The trace of a hexagonal plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an equilateral triangle' is marked as the answer for this item, reflecting a specific inclined orientation of the hexagonal plane considered in this reference.

q: 36. The length of the rectangle representing the development of the lateral surface of a right circular cylinder is equal to :
options: twice the circumference of circular base
explain: When a cylinder is 'unrolled,' the length of the resulting rectangle is the distance around the circle, which is the circumference ($2\pi r$).

q: 37. When a line is perpendicular to a reference plane, its projection on the plane to which it is perpendicular is .............
explain: A line perpendicular to a plane projects onto that plane as a single point, since the entire length of the line collapses to one location when viewed along its own axis.

q: 38. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on .............
explain: Since every face of an isometric drawing is inclined to the viewing direction, circles on any face (front, top, or side) are represented as ellipses in isometric projection.

q: 39. The illusion of depth in paintings is depicting by .............
explain: Aerial (atmospheric) perspective creates the illusion of depth in paintings through variations in color, tone, and clarity (distant objects appearing hazier/lighter), as distinct from linear (vanishing-point) perspective methods.

q: 40. In multi-view orthographic projection, the front view of a circular plane may be .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'an ellipse' is marked correct here; conventionally, depending on the plane's orientation, the front view of a circular plane can be a circle, ellipse, or straight line, so 'any one of these' would be the general case, but the given key selects option (b) for this specific item.

q: 41. A circle is in isometric projection appears as
explain: Due to the inclination of isometric faces to the line of sight, a circle is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 42. Oblique projections are of .............
explain: Oblique projections (cavalier and cabinet types) commonly use receding lines drawn at either 30° or 45° to the horizontal, so both angles are used depending on the projection type.

q: 43. In engineering drawing, auxiliary views are used to show details of .............
explain: Auxiliary views are specifically constructed to show the true shape and size of inclined (or oblique) surfaces, which appear foreshortened in the standard principal views.

q: 44. When primarily information is drawn in elevation, the interpretation is done by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'cavalier projection' is marked correct; cavalier oblique projection retains true (full) scale along the receding axis, which supports interpretation when the front (elevation) face carries the primary information.

q: 45. The most suitable angle for the cone of vision for drawing perspective is .............
explain: For a natural, undistorted perspective view, the recommended cone of vision (viewing angle) is approximately 30°, beyond which noticeable distortion occurs near the edges.

q: 46. Pictorial views are obtained by .............
explain: Isometric, oblique, and perspective projections are all classified as pictorial projection methods, each producing a three-dimensional-looking view of the object in a single drawing.

q: 47. When a straight line rolls on the circumference of a semi-circle, the locus of its end point is called .............
explain: As with a full circle, a straight line rolling without slipping along the circumference of a semicircle traces an involute curve, generalizing the involute definition to any circular arc.

q: 48. When a right circular cone is cut by a plane passing through its apex, the curve obtained is .............
explain: A section plane passing through the apex of a cone intersects it along straight generator lines meeting at the apex, producing a triangular section rather than a curved conic section.

q: 49. The angle between the asymptotes of a rectangular hyperbola is .............
explain: By definition, a rectangular (equilateral) hyperbola has its two asymptotes perpendicular to each other, meeting at 90°.

q: 50. The nature of lateral surface of cylinder is .............
explain: A cylinder's curved lateral surface bends in only one direction (around its circular cross-section) while remaining straight along its length/axis, making it a singly curved surface, unlike a sphere.
